goal: Improve the GOAT G1 UWB beacon-placement optimizer in index.html against overnight metrics: dual-coverage %, uncovered area %, beacon-link validity, runtime. Bounded at 12 iterations.

harness.loader: benchmarks/core.js extracts the inline <script> from index.html and evals it in a vm sandbox with DOM/canvas stubs (index.html stays a single file; no refactor)
scenarios: benchmarks/scenarios/los-blocker.json (80x24 m lawn split by near-full wall + tree)
harness.metrics: dual-coverage %, uncovered %, link validity (graph connected via <=45 m + LOS), blocked in-range pairs, min obstacle gap (>5 m strict), beacon count (2..10), optimizer runtime ms
harness.keep_rule: keep if worst-case dual coverage improves, or ties improve worst-case uncovered, or both tie with runtime down >3%; any spec or link-validity violation forces revert

columns_note: dual_cov_pct_best = minimum dual coverage across scenarios (worst case); uncovered_pct_worst = maximum uncovered % across scenarios; links_valid = scenarios with fully connected beacon networks; runtime_ms = sum over scenarios of optimizePlacement wall time

aggregate.note: baseline los-blocker violated the strict >5 m obstacle-gap spec; best passes all specs on all scenarios

key_findings: Baseline greedy stacked beacon 2 onto beacon 1 (spacing floor only applied from the 3rd beacon) and its early-stop accepted the degenerate stack whenever it met spec; fixed by applying the anti-cluster floor from the 2nd beacon with a small-lawn fallback (iter 1).
Candidate filter used >= 5 m for obstacle gaps but the Ecovacs spec is strictly > 5 m; a beacon at exactly 5.0 m passed in-app validation. Tightened both filter and validator (iter 1).

Brute-force oracles (bitset pair/triple enumeration over all candidates) proved the kept solutions sit at or near the constrained optimum: rect linked-pair max = 91.6% (the 92.2% 'better' pair is unlinkable), los-blocker needs >= 3 beacons (best connected pair only 72.8%).

The big coverage win was smart early termination (iter 9): keep placing while the next beacon's USEFUL gain (0->1 / 1->2 conversions, redundancy excluded) >= 3% of cells; rect went 91.6% -> 100% dual with 4 beacons, los-blocker 94.4% -> 100% with 6.
The biggest runtime win was caching {candidates, coverage lists} per geometry revision so updateJustification's coverageCurve reuses optimizePlacement's precompute (iter 6, -71%).

Two 'obvious' LOS micro-optimizations were falsified by measurement: a Map-cached bbox rejection in losClear was slower than no cache (iter 5), and hoisted-bbox alone was a wash (iter 11). Flat Float64Array edges + inlined intersection finally delivered ~7% (iter 12); an initial sign error in the inlined test silently changed coverage and was caught by the harness before commit.

files_changed.index.html: optimizer section only: strict >5 m gap (candidate filter + validate), anti-cluster spacing from 2nd beacon with fallback, incremental localRefine (wider window: 120 candidates, 0.6R, up to 5 passes), geomRev-keyed candidate/coverage cache shared with coverageCurve, quality-margin early termination, flat-edge LOS fast path in candidateCoverage
files_changed.benchmarks/core.js: new - vm-sandbox loader for the inline script
files_changed.benchmarks/AGENTS.md: new - DOX child doc for the benchmark boundary
files_changed.AGENTS.md: DOX pass: verification section + child index updated

safety: no git push, no deploy; work committed locally on main only

continuation.summary: Post-loop verification pass (optimization bound of 12 iterations unchanged): edge-case regression testing, stability gate, syntax check, one robustness fix.
continuation.edge_fix: generateCandidates now halves its step up to 4 times when zero candidates are found. Root cause investigated: on a 10x8 courtyard with a central obstacle NO valid position exists (corners are exactly 5.0 m from the obstacle, spec is strict >5 m) — baseline had the same behavior, so this was NOT an iteration regression. The fix insures against tight lawns where thin slivers are finer than the default 2 m sampling. Verified behavior-neutral on all 3 benchmark scenarios and deterministic across 5 runs.
